description:
## Description
I find the retries in this short time (3x30s=90 seconds) 
nearly useless. So i changed the rpc.py in this way
that i can do handle the retry attempts and the wait
time by configuration.

## Motivation and Context
We got "to often" the 
"RPCError: Errors (3 attempts) when connecting to remote scheduler"

## Tested?
I ran some testjobs with it and it works for me.

comments.body: Does this line really work, I thought you should replace ` %` with `,`.
Not a human readable error message. Can you come up with something that can be understood on it's own?
What? did the old code retry 3*3 times?? I see both an outer `for _ in range(attempts)` loop and a loop inside the `_fetch` function. Strange...
Hey, if you remove the kwarg `attempts` here, won't you affect other surrounding code that assumes it to be `3`??
the code didn't expect it is 3. It is set hardcoded inwith rpc.py to this number. And the default remains to 3...
I don't deepdive into the code, but when the central scheduler is not working the logging seems to explain a retry of 3
Oh, and there's nowhere it is called? If so then this is fine. :)

Actually I meant as "doesn't flake8 complain?". I think you can give the `self._rpc_retry_wait` as a parameter to the logging framework, and letting it do interpolating as a part of it's display step.
